audience_question: Which retrofit barrier is most common overall, and did service turnaround improve?
form: aligned bars, one panel per source
fit_rationale: Each source's barrier counts are one numeric measure against its own denominator, which aligned bars show directly. Separate panels keep Partner North's 40 homeowners (overlapping multi-select survey) apart from Partner South's 15 support cases, so the sources are not pooled or ranked together. Turnaround is stated as text rather than charted: it is one recent, partial median with no comparable baseline, and a chart would imply a trend the data cannot support.
tradeoff: Keeping the sources in separate panels means the slide cannot give one overall ranking of barriers; it gives a within-source answer and states that the overall question cannot be answered until the denominators are shared.
caveats: Partner North: 40 homeowners surveyed; several barriers could be selected, so counts overlap and sum to 54 rather than 40.

Partner South: 15 open support cases reviewed; homeowners served not reported; only 'waiting for an installer' (9 of 15 cases) was recorded, and the review did not record whether other barriers were present.
The two sources use different units and denominators with no shared period definition, so they cannot be pooled or ranked together.
South median turnaround is 8 days from 11 of 15 cases; 4 cases had no time recorded; the figure is recent and partial.
The note 'around two weeks last spring' gives no case count, sample or method, so it is not a comparable baseline; no improvement in turnaround is claimed.
Partner North reported no turnaround times.
Fictional scenario; all figures are invented for the evaluation.
